Dominic Sutton heads into spring with an exciting young team, led by promising new-season 3-year-olds, while an exciting bunch of new-season 2-year-olds look ready to build towards the future. While Feroce and a couple of strong staying mares add further ammunition.

Four impressive open heat winners look ready for the spring after trialling at Rosehill on Tuesday morning, with Robusto, Hidden Motive, General Salute and Reachin’ Out all impressing. While the Group 1-winner Spicy Martini was brilliant winning a trial on the Gold Coast.

From Melbourne Cup heroes returning to competition to country gallopers celebrating their 30th birthdays, TTR’s new monthly series follows retired Thoroughbreds and the lives that await them after racing. First up, Without A Fight swaps Flemington for Boneo Park, Tobacco Road marks a remarkable milestone and three Newcastle combinations secure their place at Equimillion.

Headwall’s return to The Everest conversation and Too Dardy’s breakthrough stakes victory came only after their connections committed to long, expensive and uncertain rehabilitation programs. Their trainers explain how they decided the horses were worth waiting for - and what it took to bring them back.

The first day of the Hong Kong season came with a thrilling seven-length victory by Ka Ying Rising. He smashed his own 1200-metre record by more than a second in the G3 Chief Executive’s Cup on a day when two other class records were also broken. Written Tycoon opened the season with a double.

Sunday featured Group 1 action across three major jurisdictions, and in France, it was total domination for Aga Khan Studs with a treble capped off by Erdenali's G1 Prix du Moulin de Longchamp win. Pinatubo produced his first top flight winner in the G1 Grosser Preis von Baden with Saddadd, and in the States, Hughes delivered Bob Baffert his 20th G1 Del Mar Futurity win.

Well Written completed a remarkable weekend with New Zealand racing’s highest honour, less than 24 hours after extending her unbeaten record in the G1 Proisir Plate. The rising star led an awards night that also celebrated Savabeel’s global legacy, three generations of the Williams family and Te Akau’s dominant season.

My Gladiola was asleep in her tie-up stall shortly before delivering the Group 1 win John McArdle and Kia Ora Stud had long believed was coming. The seventh foal of top racemare Villa Verde has rewarded a deal that kept her trainer in the bidding, her breeder in the ownership and may yet take them all to Royal Ascot.
